from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 7  # sources
    J = 9  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [176, 236, 182, 175, 94, 208, 250]
    demands = [57, 42, 43, 57, 56, 34, 24, 51, 18]
    cost_matrix = [[16.25, 6.14, 17.76, 4.11, 5.91, 21.09, 27.45, 11.83, 8.47], [29.09, 10.03, 18.81, 3.36, 28.02, 5.66, 13.53, 19.24, 6.72], [21.23, 27.38, 15.95, 7.49, 22.25, 6.56, 3.56, 18.33, 13.63], [7.0, 5.01, 26.94, 8.02, 11.72, 27.32, 21.46, 26.52, 29.3], [10.14, 21.0, 12.53, 24.29, 4.3, 24.7, 16.04, 9.85, 12.2], [12.68, 12.35, 27.38, 17.08, 27.43, 9.55, 3.96, 13.71, 13.31], [3.19, 11.67, 22.28, 22.77, 3.26, 19.98, 19.98, 9.96, 13.47]]
    emission_matrix = [[13.03, 12.34, 11.15, 13.88, 5.22, 5.28, 13.7, 17.26, 15.15], [4.7, 14.88, 15.72, 15.12, 15.14, 12.99, 6.33, 6.75, 18.5], [4.0, 12.31, 15.74, 16.74, 8.96, 12.21, 16.48, 12.68, 8.96], [14.48, 8.75, 3.04, 17.96, 16.73, 1.0, 16.01, 1.56, 2.1], [14.09, 16.25, 3.45, 11.78, 14.94, 2.99, 11.77, 4.57, 14.71], [14.87, 9.44, 8.18, 9.4, 12.04, 15.83, 5.56, 9.89, 13.25], [14.88, 18.08, 9.47, 6.58, 20.0, 14.52, 13.44, 9.66, 15.45]]
    fixed_costs = [[143, 292, 159, 189, 188, 138, 190, 272, 129], [195, 198, 103, 132, 164, 227, 149, 161, 91], [288, 120, 172, 278, 296, 180, 79, 291, 287], [163, 278, 61, 112, 287, 198, 140, 50, 234], [235, 51, 258, 126, 104, 239, 90, 230, 190], [55, 263, 75, 171, 235, 186, 188, 106, 76], [88, 127, 209, 163, 113, 65, 158, 270, 284]]
    moq = [[9, 19, 5, 6, 18, 6, 14, 17, 9], [17, 13, 11, 12, 7, 7, 8, 15, 18], [20, 10, 14, 13, 6, 12, 9, 14, 7], [11, 15, 12, 8, 13, 8, 18, 7, 16], [17, 8, 14, 9, 11, 10, 14, 11, 11], [5, 5, 5, 15, 5, 11, 14, 19, 5], [12, 9, 10, 6, 9, 8, 10, 7, 20]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: EVP, Supply Chain and Operations; CFO; Head of Sustainability
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Shipping plan that balances cost and carbon across our warehouse-to-store network
Date: Today

Context
Our distribution network relies on multiple warehouses serving multiple stores. Each shipping route is characterized by both a monetary cost per unit and a carbon intensity per unit. In many cases, the least expensive routes tend to have higher emissions, which creates a trade-off between cost control and our sustainability commitments. To reflect management priorities, we will use a weighted approach that values cost more than emissions while still holding ourselves accountable for carbon performance.

Operational rules and real-world constraints
- Route activation and setup fees: A shipping route must be explicitly opened before use. Opening a route triggers a one-time setup fee that covers carrier onboarding, customs or compliance paperwork, scheduling, and dock configuration. This fee applies in full whenever we use that route, regardless of the shipped volume.
- Minimum order quantities on active routes: Once a route is active, we must ship at least a specified minimum number of units on that lane. This reflects carrier requirements and the need to run full loads; small “top-off” moves are not accepted on these lanes.
- Limit on suppliers per store: Each store can receive deliveries from only a limited number of warehouses. This cap protects dock capacity, limits scheduling complexity, and respects existing vendor agreements. It also promotes volume consolidation to reduce empty miles.
- Supply and demand coverage: Every warehouse has finite inventory available for outbound shipments, and each store has a required demand that must be fulfilled. The plan cannot exceed warehouse supply or leave any store short.

Management priority and evaluation method
- We will evaluate candidate shipping plans using a blended score that reflects both variable shipping spend and total emissions, aligned with the management weights where cost has greater importance than emissions.
- Variable shipping costs and emissions are combined according to the provided weights to produce this blended score.
- One-time setup fees for any routes we choose to activate are added in full on top of the blended score. These fees are not discounted or scaled by the weights.

Business goal
Our goal is to decide which routes to activate and the shipment quantities on each active route so that:
- Warehouse inventory is not exceeded
- Each store’s demand is met in full
- Activated routes carry at least the minimum order quantities
- Each store receives product from no more than the allowed number of warehouses
- The overall blended impact—weighted variable costs plus weighted emissions, with route setup fees added in full—is kept as low as practicable

This approach will provide a clear, executable shipping plan that names the routes to open, the volumes to move on each, and the expected financial and carbon outcomes. It will also make the trade-offs transparent so leadership can confirm the current weighting or adjust it as policy and market conditions evolve.

Next steps
- Confirm warehouse supplies, store demands, and the latest per-route cost and carbon data.
- Populate the data template in the annex.
- Run scenarios to illustrate the trade-offs between lower cost and lower emissions under the operational rules above.
- Present the recommended plan, along with sensitivity to alternative weights and supplier caps, for decision.
